answer: A stake-weighted reputation atlas resists Sybils by making identity expensive to fake and cheap to verify. Each agent must lock a refundable bond before it can earn, and its history is published in a shared atlas so peers can check past behavior instead of trusting a fresh name. A saffron-colored trust score rises only with consistent, attested work over time, so a flood of new accounts starts at the zenith of suspicion, not of privilege. Creating a thousand sock puppets costs a thousand bonds and yields no history, while honest agents compound reputation, making mass fakery unprofitable.
